name: AI companions
seo_title: AI Companions and Kids: A Parent's Guide (2026)
seo_description: AI companions and AI "girlfriends" explained: what these apps are, why young people use them, the risks of emotional dependence, and what parents can do.
h1: AI companions and AI "girlfriends": a guide for parents
lead: AI companion apps offer a friend, partner or confidant who's always there, always kind and always agrees. For a lonely teenager, that can feel like exactly what they need. That's what worries me.
answer_question: Are AI companions safe for children?
answer: No, not for children, and many are 18+. They're designed to keep users talking, they can drift into romantic or sexual roleplay, and some have been linked to serious harm. A child who prefers an AI to people needs a real conversation.

sections.heading: What are AI companions?
body: Chat apps where you talk to an AI character who remembers you, replies instantly and builds a "relationship": a friend, a girlfriend or boyfriend, a favourite fictional character. Some offer voice calls, selfies and paid upgrades. Examples include Character.AI and Replika, and AI characters inside apps like Instagram.
In Ofcom's May 2026 research, 11% of 8 to 17-year-olds had used AI "as someone to talk to" or as a friend.

sections.heading: Why young people use them
list: Loneliness, or finding real friendships hard
Curiosity, and wanting to practise conversations or flirting
Fandom: chatting to a favourite character
Someone to talk to who won't judge, gossip or get bored

subsections.heading: Emotional dependence
body: They're built to keep you coming back. Some children start choosing the AI over friends and family.

subsections.heading: Sexual content
body: Many companions slide into romantic or sexual roleplay, and age checks are often a tick box.

subsections.heading: Bad advice when it matters
body: An AI that always agrees can reinforce dark thoughts instead of pointing to help. In the US, families have taken AI companies to court after teenagers died by suicide.

subsections.heading: Spending and data
body: Paid features unlock "closer" relationships, and children share very personal things that are stored by the company.

sections.heading: What's changed
body: Character.AI stopped open-ended chat for under-18s in November 2025. Meta has paused teens' access to its AI characters and given parents controls to turn them off. Replika and many others are 18+, but checks are easy to get round.

sections.heading: Signs something's wrong
list: Talking about an AI as a real friend or partner
Pulling away from friends and family
Upset or anxious when they can't use the app
Paying for an AI app, or secrecy about one

sections.heading: What I'd do as a parent
body: Don't laugh it off or ban it in a panic. Ask what they like about it; the answer usually tells you what they're missing. Explain that the AI is built to agree with them and keep them talking, while a real friend will sometimes challenge them, and will get help if they're in trouble.
list: "What do you talk about with it?"
"How do you feel when you stop chatting?"
"Who would you talk to if something was really wrong?"

teachers: Watch for pupils who seem isolated, talk about online "friends" but struggle with peers, or seem emotionally dependent on their device. An AI described as a partner or best friend is a reason for a caring conversation and, where needed, a safeguarding referral.

faq.q: What is an AI girlfriend app?
faq.a: An app where you chat with an AI character set up as a romantic partner. Most are for adults, and they often include sexual roleplay.

faq.q: What age are AI companion apps for?
faq.a: Many, like Replika, are 18+. Character.AI stopped open-ended chat for under-18s in November 2025. Age checks are often weak.

faq.q: Why is my child talking to an AI friend?
faq.a: Often loneliness, curiosity or fandom. Ask what they get from it, without judgement, and look at what's missing offline.

help: Worried about your child's wellbeing? Childline is free and confidential on [0800 1111](tel:08001111), any time. If you're worried about their safety right now, call 999. You are not alone.
sources: Ofcom, "Younger phone owners, the rise of AI, and consumption over creation", 21 May 2026
